messages:
Anya: heads up — we just got a burn-rate alert for token-latency SLOs on /text/generate (prod-eu). p95 token latency jumped ~2.5x after the kernel auto-select tweak rolled out at ~03:20 :warning:
Max: :eyes: seeing the alert. is this the kernel switch or batching tweaks? any KV cache changes?
Anya: rollout included kernel auto-select + smaller batching window for low-latency routes. KV cache config unchanged AFAIK. raw numbers: p50 12ms -> 18ms, p95 37ms -> 95ms, tail 300ms -> 820ms. burn_rate ~2.7 over 5m.
Chloe: I flipped the kernel-auto-select flag as part of the canary. I can revert if we think it's the cause. status: canary on 10% traffic in eu, 100% in canary group.
Jordan: posting quick profiler results from the canary pool sampling (5k requests):
```
# hotspot summary (top kernels by time)
int8_matmul_kernel_v2  42%
fp16_attention_fused    21%
kv_cache_lookup         9%
dispatch/serialize      6%
other                   22%
```
Max: kv_cache hit-rate on the affected route dropped from 0.87 -> 0.63 in the same window. looks correlated. maybe the kernel change altered batching pattern so more cache misses due to partial prefixes.
Anya: interesting — could be batching heuristics interacting with kernel selection. If kernel picks a different path, it may shorten the prefix that gets cached or change tokenization alignments.
Chloe: I already queued a rollback for the canary to the previous kernel selector at 03:45. deploy-bot: rolled back canary kernel-auto-select -> stable at 03:46.
deploy-bot: Deploy: kernel-selector rollback (canary) succeeded.
sre-bot: Alert: PROD token-latency-burnrate (/text/generate, prod-eu) exceeded threshold. burn_rate=2.8 over 5m — page on-call.
Jordan: for follow-up, proposing we add a per-route token-latency heatmap in Ops dashboard (time vs token-index) and a per-route SLI that slices by kv_cache_hit boolean. That would help disambiguate cache vs kernel issues.
Max: agreed. example PromQL for token-level p95 by token index (prototype):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_ms_bucket{route="\/text\/generate"}[5m])) by (le, token_index))
```
Anya: also want an anomaly detector on per-route token-index patterns. small bump across all tokens = different root cause than tail spike at high token indices. we should train a simple seasonal model on baseline heatmaps and alert on KL divergence > threshold.
Chloe: action items: 1) Jordan to add per-route heatmap and kv_hit slice to the dashboard; 2) Max to run deeper profile comparing stable vs canary (nvprof/pprof traces) and check batching distribution; 3) Anya to tune burn-rate alert to include token-index weighting so pages only on tail regressions.
Jordan: I'll add a low-cost dashboard card (GRAFANA): per-route token-heatmap, kv_hit_rate overlay, p50/p95 lines. I'll also add an alert rule: alert if burn_rate > 2 for 5m AND p95 tail (> token_index 128) increases > 1.5x.
Max: running sampling profiler now. initial difference: canary shows a 30% increase in kernel-switch overhead per request, and batching size distribution shifted left (mean batch size 3 -> 1.8). that explains more KV misses.
Anya: ok rollback stabilized p95 back down to ~40ms 10 minutes post-rollback. please keep collecting traces for postmortem.
Chloe: noted. I'll add the postmortem draft in #postmortems after we have profiles + dashboard links.
Anya: thanks all. once Jordan wires the heatmap we'll reduce noisy paging. tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
